fact_sheet.business_description: Flex designs and manufactures complex products, with a recently announced intent to separate its Cloud and Power Infrastructure segment into an independent, publicly traded company [D01]. This infrastructure business provides integrated power, thermal, and infrastructure systems specifically for AI data centers [D01].
segments_and_separable_assets: Cloud and Power Infrastructure: Focuses on AI data center infrastructure; comprises 22 engineering/manufacturing centers [D02, D03].
Remaining Manufacturing: Comprises over 75 manufacturing/logistics sites across 30 countries [D02].

drivers.driver: The market is failing to credit the full potential of the Cloud and Power Infrastructure segment, unfairly discounting it due to short-term hyperscaler concentration and separation cost concerns [D05].

The upcoming Q1 2027 spin-off acts as a definitive catalyst to unlock sum-of-the-parts value, allowing the high-growth infrastructure unit to re-rate closer to its true peer multiples [D01, D03, D07].
The valuation offers a compelling setup, with a base case target of $225 per share versus a hard floor of $145 derived from the core manufacturing business [D03, D04].
Management, led by CEO Revathi Advaithi, has already demonstrated alignment with shareholder interests by gaining unanimous board approval for the separation [D03, D07].

final.memo:
Flex designs and manufactures complex products, yet the market currently misprices the company by failing to distinguish between its stable manufacturing legacy and its rapidly scaling, high-value Cloud and Power Infrastructure segment [D01]. With the announced spin-off slated for Q1 2027, the company is on a clear path to simplifying its structure and unlocking value that is currently buried under hyperscaler concentration and operational scaling concerns [D01, D03, D05].

Our sum-of-the-parts analysis, which applies an 18x multiple to the estimated $1.2 billion in 2027 EBITDA for the infrastructure unit and a 10x multiple to the remaining manufacturing business, suggests an intrinsic value of $225 per share [D03]. This stands in stark contrast to the current trading price of $162.07, providing an attractive risk/reward skew as the market begins to appreciate the distinct margin and growth profile of the AI-focused infrastructure asset [D04, D06].

Management, led by CEO Revathi Advaithi, has moved decisively by securing unanimous board approval for this separation [D03]. Unlike many situations requiring public agitation, our role here is to support the board’s established P0 plan while monitoring execution milestones over the next three quarters [D03, D07]. We expect that the market's current fixation on separation costs and temporary working capital requirements will subside as the entity nears its independent trading date [D05].

Risks include potential execution slippage or the accumulation of stranded overhead costs, which we define as a kill criterion should they exceed 15% of projected standalone EBITDA [D05, D07]. However, we view the core manufacturing business at an 8x multiple as providing a hard valuation floor near $145 [D02, D04]. We are initiating a 5% position in the common stock, effectively utilizing our expertise in compute-capex supply chains to capture the re-rating as the separation narrative gains traction [D08].
